articleTitle: UPPER AND LOWER BOUNDS FOR HIGHER MOMENTS OF THETA FUNCTIONS
abstract: We obtain optimal lower bounds for moments of theta functions. On the other hand, we also get new upper bounds on individual theta values and moments of theta functions on average over primes. The upper bounds are based on bounds of character sums and, in particular, on a modification of some recent results of M. Z. Garaev.

articleTitle: STABLE PAIR INVARIANTS OF SURFACES AND SEIBERG–WITTENINVARIANTS
abstract: The moduli space of stable pairs on a local surface<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X=K_S$</tex> is in generalnon-compact. The action of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ {\mathbb{C}}^{\ast }$</tex> on thefibres of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>induces an action on the moduli space and the stable pairinvariants of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>are defined by the virtual localization formula. We studythe contribution to these invariants of stable pairs (schemetheoretically) supported in the zero section<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S \subsetX$</tex>. Sometimes there areno other contributions, for example, when the curve class<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex> is irreducible.We relate these surface stable pair invariants to the Poincaréinvariants of Dürr–Kabanov–Okonek. The latter are equal tothe Seiberg–Witten invariants of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex> by the work ofDürr–Kabanov–Okonek and Chang–Kiem. We give two applicationsof our result. (1) For irreducible curve classes the GW/PTcorrespondence for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X =K_S$</tex> implies Taubes'GW/SW correspondence for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex>. (2) When<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p_g(S) =0$</tex>, the difference ofsurface stable pair invariants in class<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex> and<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_S - \beta$</tex> is a universaltopological expression.

articleTitle: PARABOLIC BUNDLES OVER THE PROJECTIVE LINE AND THE DELIGNE–SIMPSON PROBLEMS
abstract: In ‘Quantization of Hitchin's Integrable System and Hecke Eigensheaves’, Beilinson and Drinfeld introduced the ‘very good’ property for a smooth complex equidimensional stack. They prove that for a semisimple group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb {C}$</tex>, the moduli stack <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text {Bun}_G(X)$</tex> of G-bundles over a smooth complex projective curve <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> is ‘very good’, as long as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> has genus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g > 1$</tex>. In the case of the projective line, when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g = 0$</tex>, this is not the case. However, the result can sometimes be extended to the projective line by introducing additional parabolic structure at a collection of marked points and slightly modifying the definition of a ‘very good’ stack. We provide a sufficient condition for the moduli stack of parabolic vector bundles over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb {P}^1$</tex> to be very good. We then use this property to study the space of solutions to the Deligne–Simpson problem.

articleTitle: BASIC MORITA EQUIVALENCES AND A CONJECTURE OF SASAKI FOR COHOMOLOGY OF BLOCK ALGEBRAS OF FINITE GROUPS
abstract: We show, using basic Morita equivalences between block algebras of finite groups, that the Conjecture of H. Sasaki from [H. Sasaki, Cohomology of block ideals of finite group algebras and stable elements, Alg. Repres. Theory16 (2013), 1039–1049] is true for a new class of blocks called nilpotent covered blocks. When this Conjecture is true, we define some transfer maps between cohomology of block algebras and analyze them through transfer maps between Hochschild cohomology algebras.

articleTitle: EGYPTIAN FRACTIONS WITH ODD DENOMINATORS
abstract: The number of solutions of the diophantine equation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sum _{i=1}^k {1}/{x_i}=1,$</tex> in particular when the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x_i$</tex> are distinct odd positive integers is investigated. The number of solutions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S(k)$</tex> in this case is, for odd <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>:<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\[ \exp \left( \exp \left( c_1 \frac{k}{\log k}\right)\right) \leq S(k) \leq \exp ( \exp(c_2 k )) \]$$</tex>with some positive constants <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c_1$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c_2$</tex>. This improves upon an earlier lower bound of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S(k) \geq \exp ((1+o(1))({\log 2}/{2})k^2)$</tex>.

articleTitle: ISOMETRIES BETWEEN SPACES OF REAL POLYNOMIALS OF DEGREE AT MOST n
abstract: Given real Banach spaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex>, we show that every isometric isomorphism from the space of approximable polynomials of degree at most <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex> to the space of approximable polynomials of degree at most <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> has the form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T(P)(y) = \pm \bar {P} \circ r^t \circ J_F(y)$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar {P}$</tex> is the Aron–Berner extension of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex> is an isometry of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E'$</tex> onto <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F'$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J_F$</tex> is the canonical inclusion of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> into <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F''$</tex>. With additional conditions on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex>, we are also able to characterize the isometric isomorphisms between the spaces of integral polynomials of degree at most <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> and the isometric isomorphisms between the spaces of all polynomials of degree at most <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>.

articleTitle: MODERATE AND LARGE DEVIATIONS FOR THE ERDŐS–KAC THEOREM
abstract: The Erdös–Kac theorem is a celebrated result in number theory which says that the number of distinct prime factors of a uniformly chosen random integer satisfies a central limit theorem. In this paper, we establish the large deviations and moderate deviations for this problem in a very general setting for a wide class of additive functions.

articleTitle: COMMUTATORS AND SQUARE-ZERO ELEMENTS IN BANACH ALGEBRAS
abstract: Our initial result states that, in a certain class of Banach algebras which includes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^*$</tex>-algebras and group algebras of locally compact groups, every commutator lies in the closed linear span of square-zero elements. The proof relies on the theory of Banach algebras with property <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb {B}}$</tex>. We then study several variations and extensions of this result. For instance, we show that in a von Neumann algebra every commutator is actually a finite sum of square-zero elements. We also consider the commutator ideal and the existence of some special square-zero elements.

articleTitle: THE CONGRUENCE η* ON SEMIGROUPS
abstract: In this paper, we define a congruence <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\eta ^{\ast }$</tex> onsemigroups. For the finite semigroups <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex>,<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\eta ^{\ast}$</tex> is the smallest congruence relation suchthat <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S/\eta ^{\ast}$</tex> is a nilpotent semigroup (in the sense ofMal'cev). In order to study the congruence relation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\eta ^{\ast}$</tex> on finite semigroups, we define a<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textbf{CS}$</tex>-diagonal finite regular Rees matrixsemigroup. We prove that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex> is a<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textbf{CS}$</tex>-diagonal finite regular Rees matrixsemigroup, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S/\eta ^{\ast }$</tex> is inverse. Also, if<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex> is a completely regular finitesemigroup, then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S/\eta ^{\ast }$</tex> is a Cliffordsemigroup.We show that, for every non-null principal factor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A/B$</tex> of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex>, there is a special principal factor<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C/D$</tex> such that every element of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A{\setminus } B$</tex> is<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\eta^{\ast }$</tex>-equivalent with some element of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C{\setminus } D$</tex>. We call the principalfactor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C/D$</tex> the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\eta ^{\ast}$</tex>-root of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A/B$</tex>.All <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\eta ^{\ast}$</tex>-roots are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textbf{CS}$</tex>-diagonal. If certain elements of<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex> act in the special way on the<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textbf{R}$</tex>-classes of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textbf{CS}$</tex>-diagonal principal factor, then it is notan <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\eta ^{\ast}$</tex>-root. Some of these results are alsoexpressed in terms of pseudovarieties of semigroups.

articleTitle: GAPS BETWEEN ZEROS OF DEDEKIND ZETA-FUNCTIONS OF QUADRATIC NUMBER FIELDS. II
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> be a quadratic number field and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\zeta _K(s)$</tex> be the associated Dedekind zeta-function. We show that there are infinitely many gaps between consecutive zeros of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\zeta _K(s)$</tex> on the critical line which are <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$>$</tex>2.866 times the average spacing.

articleTitle: ON EXPONENTIAL SUMS INVOLVING COEFFICIENTS OF L-FUNCTIONS FOR SL(3, ℤ) OVER PRIMES
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L(s,F)$</tex> be the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-function associated with a Hecke–Maass form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm SL}(3, {\mathbb {Z}})$</tex>, with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_F(n,1)$</tex> denoting the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>th coefficient of the Dirichlet series for it. It is proved that, for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N\ge 2$</tex> and any <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha \in {\mathbb {R}}$</tex>, there exists an effective constant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c >0$</tex> such that<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\[ \sum_{n\le N} \Lambda(n)A_F(n,1)e(n\alpha)\ll N \exp(-c\sqrt{\log N}), \]$$</tex>where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Lambda (n)$</tex> is the von Mangoldt function, and the implied constant depends only on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex>.

articleTitle: ORTHOGONALLY ADDITIVE AND MULTIPLICATIVE POLYNOMIALS AND HOLOMORPHIC MAPS BETWEEN FOURIER ALGEBRAS
abstract: We study the structure of a holomorphic map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H:B_{A(G_1)}(0;r)\to A(G_2)$</tex> from an open ball of a Fourier algebra into another Fourier algebra. Among other results, we show that there exist a piecewise affine homeomorphism <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma : G_2\to G_1$</tex> and a sequence <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{\omega _n\}$</tex> in the Fourier–Stieltjes algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B(G_2)$</tex> such that<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\[ H(f)(y) = \sum_{n\geq 1} \omega_n(y)f(\sigma(y))^n\quad\forall f\in B_{A(G_1)}(0;r), \]$$</tex>when the locally compact groups <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G_1, G_2$</tex> are amenable and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex> is completely bounded, orthogonally additive and multiplicative, and conformal.

articleTitle: WEAKLY METRIZABILITY OF SPHERES AND RENORMINGS OF BANACH SPACES
abstract: We study the metrizability of weak topologies when restricted to the unit sphere of some equivalent norm on a Banach space, and its relationships with other geometrical properties of norms. In case of dual Banach space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X^{\ast },$</tex> we prove that there exists a dual norm such that its unit sphere is weak<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\ast }$</tex> metrizable if and only if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathscr {B}_{X^{\ast }},w^{\ast })$</tex> is a descriptive compact, which provides a complete characterization.

articleTitle: DUAL SPACES OF MULTI-PARAMETER MARTINGALE HARDY SPACES
abstract: In this paper, we introduce the generalized multi-parameter martingale <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$BMO$</tex> spaces. The atomic decomposition of the multi-parameter martingale Hardy–Lorentz space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{p,q}^s$</tex> is given. With the help of this, the dual space of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{p,q}^s$</tex> is characterized as the generalized <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$BMO$</tex> space. Finally, as an application, the John–Nirenberg inequality is generalized for multi-parameters.

articleTitle: DUALITY IN SPACES OF LORCH ANALYTIC MAPPINGS
abstract: For a complex Banach algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex>, we study the strong dual of the Fréchet space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathcal {H}}_L(E)$</tex> of the mappings <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f: E \rightarrow E$</tex> that are analytic in the sense of Lorch. First, we will show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathcal {H}_L(E)^\prime , \beta )$</tex> is isomorphic to a regular inductive limit of Banach spaces of sequences in the strong dual of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex>. As a consequence, we will get topological properties of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathcal {H}_L(E)^\prime , \beta )$</tex> and we will show that this strong dual is the inductive dual of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {H}_L(E)$</tex>.

articleTitle: EXTREME VALUES OF THE ZETA FUNCTION AT CRITICALPOINTS
abstract: We consider large and small values of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|\zeta (\rho _1)|$</tex> when<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\zeta'(\rho _1)=0$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Re} \rho _1 >1$</tex>.

articleTitle: AN ABSTRACT MORIMOTO THEOREM FOR GENERALIZED F-STRUCTURES
abstract: We abstract Morimoto's construction of complex structures on product manifolds to pairs of certain generalized <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex>-structures on manifolds that are not necessarily global products. Using our Abstract Morimoto Theorem, we give a characterization of invariant generalized complex structures on products in which one factor is a Lie group. As a second application, we extend a theorem of Blair, Ludden and Yano on Hermitian bicontact manifolds to the non-commutative case.

articleTitle: JACOBIAN VARIETY OF GENERALIZED FERMAT CURVES
abstract: The isogenous decomposition of the Jacobian variety of classical Fermat curve of prime degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p \geq 5$</tex> has been obtained by Aoki using techniques of number theory, by Barraza and Rojas in terms of decompositions of the algebra of groups, and by Hidalgo and Rodríguez using Kani–Rosen results. In the last, it was seen that all factors in the isogenous decomposition are Jacobian varieties of certain cyclic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-gonal curves. The highest Abelian branched covers of an orbifold of genus 0 with exactly <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n+1$</tex> branch points, each one of order <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>, are provided by the so-called generalized Fermat curves of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(p,n)$</tex>; these being a suitable fiber product of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n-1$</tex> Fermat curves of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>. In this paper, we provide a decomposition, up to isogeny, of the Jacobian variety of a generalized Fermat curve <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex> of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(p,n)$</tex> as a product of Jacobian varieties of certain cyclic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-gonal curves, whose explicit equations are provided in terms of the equations for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex>. As a consequence of this decomposition, we are able to provide explicit positive-dimensional families of closed Riemann surfaces whose Jacobian variety is isogenous to the product of elliptic curves.

articleTitle: Tensor products of monotone complete $C^{\ast }$-algebras
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {A}\,{\bar {\otimes }}\,L(K)$</tex> be the Fubini product of a monotone complete <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^{\ast }$</tex>-algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {A}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L(K)$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> is an arbitrary Hilbert space. Hamana defined a product ‘<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\circ $</tex>’ in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {A}\,{\bar {\otimes }}\,L(K),$</tex> which turns <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathcal {A}\,{\bar {\otimes }}\,L(K),\circ )$</tex> into a monotone complete <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^{\ast }$</tex>-algebra. To help him to do this, he introduced a new concept of order convergence, which is subtly different from Kadison–Pedersen convergence, and, made use of the Choi–Effros product related to a completely positive idempotent map on the injective envelope of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>, whose existence is a consequence of Zorn's lemma. When <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> is separable, Saitô and Wright showed that the algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathcal {A}\,{\bar {\otimes }}\,L(K),\circ )$</tex> is the quotient algebra of the Borel tensor pro- duct <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {A}^{\infty } \,{\bar {\otimes }}\,L(K)$</tex> of the Pedersen–Baire envelope <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {A}^{\infty }$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L(K)$</tex> by a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma $</tex>-ideal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I$</tex>. In this paper, when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> is separable, it is shown, by making use of Kadison–Pedersen convergence, that there is a natural monotone <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma $</tex>-closed two-sided ideal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {A}^{\infty }\,{\bar {\otimes }}\,L(K)$</tex>, such that the quotient algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {B} =\mathcal {A}^{\infty }\,{\bar {\otimes }}\,L(K)/J$</tex> is monotone <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma $</tex>-complete, and the quotient map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q_{J}$</tex> restricts to a unital iso- metric bijection <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Phi $</tex> from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {A}\,{\bar {\otimes }}\,L(K)$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {B}$</tex>. Via the map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Phi $</tex>, we can transplant the multiplication on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {B}$</tex> into the multiplication ‘<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bullet $</tex>’ on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {A}\bar {\otimes }L(K)$</tex> so that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathcal {A}\,{\bar {\otimes }}\,L(K),\bullet )$</tex> is a monotone complete <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C^{\ast }$</tex>-algebra. It is also shown that the product ‘<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bullet $</tex>’ coincides with ‘<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\circ $</tex>’ (and so <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I=J$</tex>). So there is no need to appeal to Zorn's lemma here for our approach to defining the product ‘<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\circ $</tex>’. Our construction sheds some fresh light on classification problems of cross product algebras associated with generic dynamics.

articleTitle: ORIENTATION-PRESERVING YOUNG MEASURES
abstract: We prove a characterization result in the spirit of the Kinderlehrer–Pedregal Theorem for Young measures generated by gradients of Sobolev maps satisfying the orientation-preserving constraint, that is, the pointwise Jacobian is positive almost everywhere. The argument to construct the appropriate generating sequences from such Young measures is based on a variant of convex integration in conjunction with an explicit lamination construction in matrix space. Our generating sequence is bounded in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm L}^p$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> less than the space dimension, a regime in which the pointwise Jacobian behaves flexibly, as is illustrated by our results. On the other hand, for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> larger than or equal to the space dimension the situation necessarily becomes rigid and a construction as presented here cannot succeed. Applications to relaxation of integral functionals, the theory of semiconvex hulls and approximation of weakly orientation-preserving maps by strictly orientation-preserving ones in Sobolev spaces are given.

articleTitle: LIMIT POINTS AND LONG GAPS BETWEEN PRIMES
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_n := p_{n+1} - p_n$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p_n$</tex> denotes the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>th smallest prime, and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R(T) := \log T \log _2 T\log _4 T/ (\log _3 T)^2$</tex> (the ‘Erdös–Rankin’ function). We consider the sequence <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(d_n/R(p_n))$</tex> of normalized prime gaps, and show that its limit point set contains at least <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$25\%$</tex> of non-negative real numbers. We also show that the same result holds if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R(T)$</tex> is replaced by any ‘reasonable’ function that tends to infinity more slowly than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R(T)\log _3 T$</tex>. We also consider ‘chains’ of normalized prime gaps. Our proof combines breakthrough work of Maynard and Tao on bounded gaps between primes with subsequent developments of Ford, Green, Konyagin, Maynard and Tao on long gaps between consecutive primes.

articleTitle: The A-Stokes approximation for non-stationary problems
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal A$</tex> be an elliptic tensor. A function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf {v}\in L^1(I;{\rm LD}_{{\rm div}\,}(B))$</tex> is a solution to the non-stationary <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal A $</tex>-Stokes problem iff (0.1)<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\begin{equation} \int_Q \mathbf{v}\cdot\partial_t\boldsymbol{\varphi}\,{\rm d}x\,{\rm d}t-\int_Q \mathcal A(\varepsilon(\mathbf{v}),\varepsilon(\boldsymbol{\varphi}))\,{\rm d}x=0\quad\forall\boldsymbol{\varphi}\in C^{\infty}_{0,{\rm div}\,}(Q), \end{equation}$$</tex>where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q:=I\times B$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B\subset \mathbb {R}^d$</tex> bounded. If the l.h.s. of (0.1) is not zero but small, we talk about almost solutions. We present an approximation result in the fashion of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal A$</tex>-caloric approximation for the non-stationary <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal A $</tex>-Stokes problem. Precisely, we show that every almost solution <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf {v}\in L^p(I;W^{1,p}_{{\rm div}\,}(B))$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1<p<\infty $</tex>, to (0.1) can be approximated by a solution to (0.1) in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L^s(I;W^{1,s}(B))$</tex>-sense for all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s<p$</tex>. So, we extend the stationary <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal A$</tex>-Stokes approximation from [D. Breit, L. Diening and M. Fuchs, Solenoidal Lipschitz truncation and applications in fluid mechanics, J. Differential Equations253 (2012), 1910–1942] to parabolic problems.

articleTitle: THE SHIFTED CONVOLUTION OF DIVISOR FUNCTIONS
abstract: We prove an asymptotic formula for the shifted convolution of the divisor functions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_3(n)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d(n)$</tex>, which is uniform in the shift parameter and which has a power-saving error term. The method is also applied to give analogous estimates for the shifted convolution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d_3(n)$</tex> and Fourier coefficients of holomorphic cusp forms. These asymptotics improve previous results obtained by several different authors.

articleTitle: GENERATING GROUPS USING HYPERGRAPHS
abstract: To a set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {B} $</tex> of 4-subsets of a set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega $</tex> of size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n,$</tex> we introduce an invariant called the ‘hole stabilizer’ which generalizes a construction of Conway, Elkies and Martin of the Mathieu group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M_{12}$</tex> based on Lloyd's ‘15-puzzle’. It is shown that hole stabilizers may be regarded as objects inside an objective partial group (in the sense of Chermak). We classify pairs <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\Omega ,\mathcal {B} )$</tex> with a trivial hole stabilizer, and determine all hole stabilizers associated to 2-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(n,4,\lambda )$</tex> designs with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda \leqslant 2$</tex>.

articleTitle: ANNIHILATION OF COHOMOLOGY, GENERATION OF MODULES AND FINITENESS OF DERIVED DIMENSION
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R,\mathfrak {m},k)$</tex> be a commutative noetherian local ring of Krull dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>. We prove that the cohomology annihilator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathsf {ca}\,(R)$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex> contains a power of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak {m}$</tex> if and only if, for some <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\ge 0,$</tex> the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>th syzygies in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathsf {mod}\,R$</tex> are constructed from syzygies of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> by taking direct sums/summands and a fixed number of extensions. These conditions yield that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex> is an isolated singularity such that the bounded derived category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathsf {D^b}\,(R)$</tex> and the singularity category <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathsf {D_{sg}}\,(R)$</tex> have finite dimension, and the converse holds when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex> is Gorenstein. We also show that the modules locally free on the punctured spectrum are constructed from syzygies of finite length modules by taking direct sums/summands and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> extensions. This result is exploited to investigate several ascent and descent problems between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex> and its completion <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hat R$</tex>.
